Only alerts you when protection stops while PrivacyGuard is running. It does not restart protection or block traffic.
Every alert, the weekly summary and blocklist update notices. The VPN drop alert has its own switch.
Name the app and the server in alerts. Off: notifications only say what kind of alert it is, so nothing about your apps shows on the lock screen or to apps that read notifications.
Let screenshots, screen recording and the recent-apps preview show PrivacyGuard. Off: screens with your history are blocked from them.
If PrivacyGuard crashes, start protection again within seconds. Needs Android’s Alarms & reminders access.

After a crash, Android only lets an app start its protection again from an exact alarm, and exact alarms need Alarms & reminders access. PrivacyGuard sets that alarm only after a crash, never while protection runs, so it does not wake your phone otherwise. Without it you get a “Protection stopped” notification instead.

Sends your connections through two SOCKS5 servers, so neither server knows both who you are and where you go. SOCKS5 carries TCP only; see below for what that means.

Through the chain (You → Hop 1 → Hop 2 → Internet): every TCP connection, and your DNS lookups when DoH (encrypted DNS) is on.\nNot through the chain: plain DNS when DoH is off goes straight to your resolver, so turn on DoH. QUIC (UDP port 443) is always blocked while Dual VPN is on, so apps fall back to TCP through the chain. Other UDP (calls, games, video chat) goes direct, unless you turn on the switch below.
Strict mode (%1$s) bypasses the blocklist and is blocked; set Private DNS to Off or Automatic

Minimal blocks malware and phishing hosts only. Ads and trackers load, except the ad-SDK servers that “Block ad and attribution SDKs” in “Why am I seeing this ad?” blocks (on by default). Your own rules always apply.
Standard blocks malware, ads and trackers. At every level, your own rules apply, and so does “Block ad and attribution SDKs” in “Why am I seeing this ad?” when it is on.

Strict also blocks system telemetry (Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, Mozilla, Google Safe Browsing). Some features may stop working. At every level, your own rules apply, and so does “Block ad and attribution SDKs” in “Why am I seeing this ad?” when it is on.
Drops all other UDP while Dual VPN is on, so nothing leaves without the chain. Voice and video calls and many games will stop working.
Not tested: protection is off, so DNS goes to the network’s own resolver.
%1$s did not answer a test lookup. Websites may fail to load.

To keep protection on, turn on Always-on VPN for PrivacyGuard in Android. Android then starts it after a reboot. With “Block connections without VPN” nothing goes out unprotected, but if PrivacyGuard crashes the phone is offline until PrivacyGuard restarts (Automatic restart after a crash) or you open it again.
Background use is set to Restricted, so Android can stop protection when PrivacyGuard is not on screen. Open battery settings and choose Unrestricted.
Battery optimization is on (the Android default). Some phones stop protection in the background anyway; if protection keeps turning off, set PrivacyGuard\'s battery use to Unrestricted.
Unrestricted: Android will not stop PrivacyGuard to save battery.
